newsitem.title: UK: Coffee growers oppose EU move on coffee labelling.
newsitem.headline: Coffee growers oppose EU move on coffee labelling.

text.p: Key coffee growers said on Saturday they opposed plans by the European Union and other major coffee users to re-designate the origin of coffee, saying that it would undermine the very fabric of coffee culture.

The Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC), which accounts for over 80 percent of world's output, said the EU-led initiative would involve changes for the determination of coffee origin or the place where it is grown and harvested.
In a statement issued at a meeting in London, the ACPC said the consumers were expected to present their proposals to the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
Under the proposals, coffee processed beyond a certain degree in any given EU importing country would be labelled as originating there and not in the growing country.
"Origin is one of the most important factors for the determination of the organoleptic characteristics of coffee," the ACPC statement said.

"The lack of recognition of origin (where coffee is actually planted, grown and harvested) will lead to general confusion...and could be a factor to undermine the very fabric of coffee culture," it said.

"Producing countries unanimously oppose all kinds of proposals which might lead to give coffee as a final product (green, roasted, roasted and ground, decaffeinated, soluble coffees, extracts, etc) a different origin from the one that is attributed by the place where it is produced," it added.
Producer delegates have said they were upset by the proposals and wary of them being implemented.
"We are very concerned about the proposed changes," one delegate told Reuters on Friday, adding that he considered the origin of coffee is where it is produced.
